lines: Good tools held. So did I. I'll inspect both before sleeping.
My grip held when it had to. I'll think about that for a while.
The handle held, the edge held, and I held on behind them.
I'll inspect every tool I carried. I may inspect my knees too.
A good grip saved me more than once tonight.
I made it back with work to do and hands still able to do it.
Nothing tests a tool like <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray>. Nothing tests a person faster.
I know what stress does to metal now. I know what it does to me too.
When danger came close, nobody had time to sound brave first.
You learn a lot about a village when everyone hears the bell at once.
